1.explanation: 1. BaseVector.js (src/ol/layer/BaseVector.js) introduced a new `background` option on vector layers and stores its value unconditionally, even when set to `false`.  2. MapboxVector.js (src/ol/layer/MapboxVector.js) configures that background (via ol-mapbox-style) and passes it through to the underlying VectorTile source. 3. CanvasVectorLayerRenderer.js (src/ol/renderer/canvas/VectorLayer.js) sees the layer’s background property and unconditionally calls `context.fillStyle = <background>` before drawing, without checking for boolean or undefined values. 4. colorlike.js (src/ol/colorlike.js)’s `asColorLike` simply returns non-array inputs (including `false` or `undefined`), so Canvas ends up calling the internal color parser (`fromStringInternal_`) on a non-string/invalid value, triggering the assertion. Together these cause any vector layer with a background (or a disabled background via `false`) to throw when rendered over another layer.
1.bug_scenario: A user adds a MapboxVector layer (with a background) on top of an OSM TileLayer and sees an assertion failure instead of the vector layer: “Assertion failed. See https://openlayers.org/en/latest/doc/errors/#14”. This happens in the Canvas renderer when setting up the layer’s background and it crashes in the color‐parsing code. No map image is drawn, and the console shows a stack trace through CanvasVectorLayerRenderer.useContainer → renderFrame → fromStringInternal_.
